hooks.A: The story of Nintendo: over one hundred thirty years old, and it started with playing cards.
hooks.C: The story of Nintendo: how a playing card shop almost went broke, then took over video games.

lines.text: In 1889, Fusajiro Yamauchi opened a small shop in Kyoto, Japan.
He made hanafuda, traditional Japanese playing cards.
Decades later, in 1949, a young Hiroshi Yamauchi took over the company.
He wanted to grow beyond cards, so he tried everything.
A taxi company. Love hotels. Even instant rice.
Almost all of it failed, and Nintendo came close to bankruptcy.
Then he noticed a factory maintenance worker, Gunpei Yokoi, who built a toy arm for fun.
Nintendo sold it as the Ultra Hand in 1966, and it sold over a million units.
Nintendo became a toy company, and then it moved into video games.
In 1981, an arcade game called Donkey Kong became a massive hit.
Its little hero, Jumpman, would later get a new name: Mario.
Then came the Famicom in Japan, and the NES in America, starting in 1985.
Not bad for a playing card shop from 1889.
